reviews.title: Abraham called into covenant
reviews.provisionalConclusion: Keep the Abraham call and divided-animal covenant in the existing selected Scripture. The proposed genealogy lead is already separately source-owned; Genesis 11:26–31 remains a held passage rather than becoming a new narrated event.

issues.sourceBoundedFinding: Retain the existing Sem-to-Abram connector or test the independent Genesis 11:26–31 reading; do not narrate Abram's lineage without citation or automatically promote the held text.
The divided-animal preparation is essential context for the furnace/fire passing between the divisions in Genesis 15:17–18; the already-restored verses should stay in the research reading.
Preserve the explicit circumcision covenant passage as a distinct selected witness after Genesis 15, not a repeated or synthetic covenant speech.

reviews.title: Isaac, Jacob and Israel
reviews.provisionalConclusion: Preserve Isaac's sacrifice in its continuous selected wording and the separate Jacob narrative. The omission of Jacob's dream is an editorial choice, not evidence that the dream has no place in the full Bible.

issues.sourceBoundedFinding: Retain the whole biblical trial, angelic intervention and substitute ram rather than trimming the decisive resolution; theological typology belongs outside the main narration.

The existing 151-event Atlas records Jacob's dream but the continuous P3 selection does not; test this exact source passage as a potential transition rather than reusing the Atlas record as invented narration.

The original V18 uses Genesis 32:23–33; the English installed witnesses locate the same story Genesis 32:22–32, while Crampon retains 23–33. The P3 source-reader correction now uses witness-specific spans and remains uncollated and unapproved.

The current separately attributed editorial note about Jacob receiving Isaac's blessing has proper source coordinates; do not attribute its exact wording to Genesis or silently transform the context into a verse quotation.

reviews.title: Joseph and the descent into Egypt
reviews.provisionalConclusion: The Joseph sequence is causally intelligible as selected biblical text from betrayal through the dreams' interpretation, appointment, reunion and Israel's descent; the imprisonment source remains an independent held bridge.

issues.sourceBoundedFinding: Genesis 41:14 already retrieves Joseph from confinement; the Genesis 39 prison scene can enrich the connection but must remain an independently reviewed source trial, not a synthetic episode.
Keep Joseph's interpretation, advice and Pharaoh's response in source order. Cutting advice before appointment would remove the causal justification established by the selected witness.
The brothers' reunion is linked to Israel's later descent in Genesis 46:1–7; distinguish the selected literary episode from the Atlas's broader chronological records.

reviews.title: Bondage and the calling of Moses
reviews.provisionalConclusion: The transition from Hebrew oppression to Moses' encounter at the bush remains source-attributed, but the selected main Scripture omits nearly all of Exodus 2. No replacement text may be invented.

issues.sourceBoundedFinding: The Atlas includes Moses' early preservation. Decide whether to trial exactly Exodus 2:1–10 as independent selected Scripture rather than treating the editorial bridge as a complete narrative scene.
The current context note covers flight and Israel's cry with cited Scripture. If expanded, preserve the actual Exodus 2 sequence; do not infer Moses' years or a precisely mapped Midian itinerary.
The existing 3:1–8 and 3:10–15 sources identify God's call and name. Verse 3:9 is omitted; assess this narrow elision in continuous reading without manufacturing Moses' response.

reviews.title: Plagues and the first Passover
reviews.provisionalConclusion: The Passover instructions retain their sacrificial details, but the firstborn judgment at Exodus 12:29–30 is an essential narrative transition to the next movement's midnight command to depart.

issues.sourceBoundedFinding: Pharaoh's persistent refusal is represented by independently labelled context and named sources rather than an invented summary of all ten plagues.
Protect the lamb, blood, eating and memorial wording across the current selected subspans, without treating the omitted regulations as no longer canonical.

The firstborn are slain and Egypt cries out here, immediately before Pharaoh summons Moses in Exodus 12:31. The selected M08 ends Exodus 12:28; the existing P3 manuscript has already identified these two verses as a bridge trial. Mark them highest-priority to consider for M08→M09 continuity, with no release promotion before approval.

reviews.title: Exodus through the sea
reviews.provisionalConclusion: The escape is anchored in Exodus 12 and 14. The sea sequence now preserves the Egyptians' entry before the returning water. The wilderness manna remains clearly secondary editorial context.

issues.sourceBoundedFinding: Do not imply that Pharaoh released Israel spontaneously: M08 must either disclose omitted Exodus 12:29–30 or trial that actual source, then M09 resumes with the already selected verse 12:31.

Verse 14:23 is already restored to show the Egyptian entry before the sea closes. Verses 14:24–25 are omitted from current selected Scripture; they can be considered as further source context but should not be paraphrased into a verse.

The existing Atlas contains a full manna entry; the main P3 reading retains only a source-backed editorial transition. Preserve that division unless the author accepts a direct native Scripture reading.

reviews.title: Sinai: covenant and unfaithfulness
reviews.provisionalConclusion: The Sinai reading preserves God's covenant demand, the Ten Commandments and covenant ratification, before the calf episode. The spectacular Sinai manifestation and Tabernacle's closure have different status and references.

issues.sourceBoundedFinding: The 151-event Atlas contains this theophany, but the main selected P3 reading begins Exodus 19:1–8 then the Decalogue. Test including 19:16–20 for direct-source atmosphere if required for Theatre, without treating Atlas as the text owner.
All ten commandments must remain in their attested wording; Exodus 24:3–8 independently supplies the covenant's ratification.

The original editorial note's source 40:34–38 is Crampon-numbered; its cloud scene occurs English verses 40:32–36 in both uncollated English witnesses. The research proof now displays three-edition source-specific references; no attempt to equate same verse numbers.
The selected segments preserve creation of the calf, divine anger, Moses' intercession, its destruction and Israel's accountability; maintain a named source witness, no invented divine speech.

nextDecisions: Highest priority: consider the exact Exodus 12:29–30 reading before the Pharaoh Exodus 12:31 release; avoid the gap M08→M09.
Review Genesis 28:10–22, Exodus 2:1–10, and Exodus 19:16–20 as individually sourced candidate original-Scripture trials, not broad prose expansions.
Verify Genesis 32 and Exodus 40 numbering semantically against intended printed Catholic editions; the research reader now has edition-specific pointers.
